description: TEST-ONLY mock of the backend API so the main workflow (product-video-main) can be run end-to-end inside n8n BEFORE the real backend is deployed. Import and ACTIVATE this workflow, then set the main workflow's BACKEND_URL env to https://<your-n8n-host>/webhook/mock (no trailing slash). The mock simulates job progress across polls: QUEUED -> RESEARCHING -> PLANNING -> GENERATING_ASSETS -> RENDERING -> COMPLETED (polls 1-5), so the main workflow's full validate -> create -> poll -> respond loop can be watched in ~100 seconds. HONEST LIMITS: no video is generated; the downloadUrl in the success response points at the mock and will not return a real MP4. It only proves the orchestration loop works.
name: product-video-mock-backend

nodes.name: webhook-mock-create
nodes.notes: POST {BACK}/api/v1/jobs — mimics the real job-creation endpoint. Returns { ok: true, data: { id, status: 'QUEUED' } } and resets the poll counter.

nodes.name: mock-create
nodes.notes: Mints a fake job id, resets the per-workflow poll counter in static data.

nodes.name: respond-created
nodes.notes: Returns HTTP 200 with the fake job record.

nodes.name: webhook-mock-status
nodes.notes: GET {BACK}/api/v1/jobs/:jobId — mimics the real status endpoint. Each call advances the fake pipeline so the main workflow's poll loop can be watched: poll 1 QUEUED, poll 2 RESEARCHING, poll 3 PLANNING, poll 4 GENERATING_ASSETS, poll 5 RENDERING, poll 6+ COMPLETED.

nodes.name: mock-status
nodes.notes: Counts polls in workflow static data and returns the matching fake job state with 15 stage rows, mirroring the real backend's status vocabulary.

nodes.name: respond-status
nodes.notes: Returns HTTP 200 with the fake job status.
